The Moving Average indicator is a trend following indicator that shows the average price of a financial instrument over a specified period of time. The indicator is calculated by taking the sum of the closing prices over a specified period of time and dividing that sum by the number of periods. The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator is a momentum indicator that shows the relationship between two moving averages of a financial instrument. The MACD is calculated by subtracting the 26-period exponential moving average (EMA) from the 12-period EMA. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) indicator is a momentum indicator that shows the strength of a trend in a financial instrument. The RSI is calculated by taking the average of the gains and losses over a specified period of time and dividing that average by the sum of the gains and losses. The Fibonacci Retracement indicator is a technical analysis tool that is used to identify potential areas of support and resistance in a financial instrument. The Fibonacci Retracement indicator is created by dividing the distance between two significant price points by the Fibonacci ratios of 0.236, 0.382, 0.500, 0.618, and 0.786. The Bollinger Bands indicator is a volatility indicator that shows the upper and lower limits of a financial instrument's price movement. The Bollinger Bands are calculated by taking the simple moving average (SMA) of a financial instrument's price over a specified period of time and adding and subtracting two standard deviations.
